items.question: What core temperature must cooked duck reach before release?
items.answer: Cooked duck must reach a core temperature of 75C before release.[1][3]

sources.1:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE SOP-014 Revision 3
Purpose: ensure cooked duck reaches release temperature.
Scope: all cook lines.
Procedure: probe the thickest part; product must reach 75C core before release.
Responsibilities: line supervisor.
sources.2:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE SOP-014 Revision 3

Purpose: ensure cooked duck reaches release temperature.
Scope: all cook lines.
Procedure: probe the thickest part; product must reach 75C core before release.
Responsibilities: line supervisor.
sources.3:
HACCP plan - Cooked duck

CCP 1 Cooking
Hazard: survival of pathogens.
Critical limit: core temperature of 75C or above.
Monitoring: probe every batch.
Corrective action: continue cooking and re-probe.
CCP 2 Chilling
Hazard: growth of pathogens.
Critical limit: product below 5C within 4 hours of cooking.
Monitoring: probe each trolley.
Corrective action: hold and assess the batch.
sources.4:
Example Retailer Code of Practice - Appendix A: microbiological limits at release

Product           TVC (cfu/g)    Enterobacteriaceae (cfu/g)    Listeria monocytogenes
Cooked duck       1.0E+05        1.0E+03                       Not detected in 25g
Cooked chicken    1.0E+05        1.0E+03                       Not detected in 25g
Raw poultry       1.0E+07        1.0E+04                       Not applicable
Cooked sauces     1.0E+04        1.0E+02                       Not detected in 25g
sources.5:
Example Retailer Code of Practice for Suppliers > Clause 2.1

2.1 Cooked ready to eat product shall not exceed 1.0E+05 cfu/g total viable count at release.

items.question: How often must the metal detector be checked during production?
items.answer: The metal detector must be checked at least hourly during production, and after any product change. [1][2]

sources.1:
SOP-021 Metal detection > 3. Procedure > 3.2 Hourly checks

Repeat the test piece check every hour and after any product change.
sources.2:
Example Retailer Code of Practice for Suppliers > Clause 3.2

3.2 Metal detection shall be verified at least hourly using Fe, Non-Fe and stainless test
pieces.
sources.3:
SOP-021 Metal detection > 3. Procedure > 3.1 Start-up test

At start-up pass the Fe 2.0mm, Non-Fe 2.5mm and SS 3.0mm test pieces through the
detector. All three must be rejected.
sources.4:
SOP-021 Metal detection > 4. Records

Record each check on form GF-07.
sources.5:
SOP-021 Metal detection > 1. Purpose

Ensure every pack passes through a working metal detector.

items.question: What does the retailer code of practice say about Listeria monocytogenes in ready to eat product?
items.answer: The retailer code of practice states that Listeria monocytogenes shall not be detected in 25g of ready-to-eat product [1]. The microbiological limits appendix further specifies this requirement for cooked ready-to-eat products, requiring that Listeria monocytogenes not be detected in 25g [2].

2.2 Listeria monocytogenes shall not be detected in 25g of ready to eat product.

Cooked chicken    1.0E+05        1.0E+03                       Not detected in 25g

Cooked sauces     1.0E+04        1.0E+02                       Not detected in 25g

items.question: What is the ATP swab pass limit after cleaning?
items.answer: The ATP swab pass limit after cleaning is below 150 RLU [2].

sources.1:
SOP-033 Cleaning verification > 2. Method

Take an ATP swab from five food contact surfaces after each daily clean and read the result
in relative light units (RLU).
sources.2:
SOP-033 Cleaning verification > 3. Limits

Pass: below 150 RLU. Between 150 and 300 RLU: reclean and retest. Above 300 RLU: fail,
hold the line and inform the supervisor.
sources.3:
SOP-033 Cleaning verification > 4. Records

Record every swab result on form GF-19.
sources.4:
SOP-033 Cleaning verification > 1. Purpose

Confirm that food contact surfaces are clean after the daily clean.
